verdict.rationale: Fly.io documents real sandbox isolation for agent work. Sprites are hardware-isolated, egress-locked, disposable VMs with a clean baseline per request, built for running untrusted code and evals, with checkpoint and rollback and per-Sprite scoping of service access. However, the evidence never describes a dedicated test or staging environment that is guaranteed to be separated from production data, such as a database branch or masked copy. That isolation from production is only implied by VM isolation and access scoping. missing for 10: explicit documentation of test/staging environments isolated from production data (e.g. database branching or sandboxed data copies), independent hands-on corroboration of the sandbox workflow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Run it in a hardware-isolated VM. A clean baseline per request, so no two users ever share state. Egress-locked and disposable.
Run untrusted code, evals, and RL rollouts in parallel. Checkpoint what works, throw away the rest.
Give your agent its own hardware-isolated Linux computer.
Roll back to any checkpoint in seconds
Grant access on purpose: by Sprite name, by label, or down to a single endpoint
